text.p: Champion Enterprises Inc said Monday that first quarter earnings are estimated to be about $0.28 per share, comparable to 1996 first quarter earnings per share, but less than the current analysts' consensus of $0.32 per share.
The company said first quarter sales revenues are estimated to be about 10 percent higher than last year, including results of the companies acquired in 1996.
The company said its Redman Indiana operations experienced reduced sales and income due to restructuring of its product line during the quarter.
In addition Champion said it incurred startup expenses at three operations, two in Indiana and one in Alabama.

The effects of these items will reduce first quarter income by about $0.04 per share, Champion said. As a result, earnings per share for the quarter will approximate last year's results, Champion said.
Champion said the level of retail activity, backed by strong consumer confidence and job creation bodes well for the year as we enter the spring retail selling season.

Assuming that industry wholesale shipments grow four to seven percent in 1997, the company said it estimates its full year earnings will be in the range of $1.62 to $1.67 per share, compared with 1996 earnings of $1.43 per share, excluding nonrecurring charges of $0.34 per share.
